decisions.reason: Definition (a) exhaustively listed permitted configuration entries but omitted the linear tangent-space isometry required by (b)3. Parameters and annotations supplied no reconstruction of that map, so the promised deflection case had no admissible configuration. Added an explicit metric-preserving linear-isomorphism entry and made (b)3 consume it with Phi(n_1)=n_2. This is a missing input type in a nonproof definition, classified other. Also corrected the spatial-projection locator from supplier clause (b) to (c).

Statement (ii)1 included transported clocks but identified only apparatus and analysis as missing after naming static-Schwarzschild and comoving-FLRW predictions. Their inspected statements restrict the observer velocities and do not calculate arbitrary transported-clock comparisons. This is a nonfatal omission from a future research queue, with no present comparison or proof depending on it. Repaired the queue to require a trajectory-specific proper-time comparison at reunion, or the actual moving-observer signal-frequency prediction, in addition to apparatus and analysis. Will section 2.1.3 separately discusses moving-clock effects; only its relevant survey passage was consulted, not a primary experimental report.

reviews.reason: The supplied linear isomorphism preserves the metric and maps n_1 to n_2; hence it maps n_1-perp to n_2-perp and preserves the positive rest-space norm. The nonzero projected vectors give a positive denominator, and the cited Cauchy-Schwarz inequality bounds kappa in [-1,1], within the principal arccos domain. Checked the observer/projection definition and decomposition lemma directly. No identification existence or canonical transport is asserted; all other readouts, conditional interpretation, hard boxes, and absence of statistical guarantees are retained. This is the adjudicator check of its repair, not an independent review.

Reviewed the queue against the repaired architecture, the exact static and comoving redshift theorem Statements, the proper-time definition (d), and ideal-clock postulate (i). The two redshift theorems concern energies along rays with specified observer congruences, not differences of clock durations along arbitrary timelike segments. The revised queue distinguishes reunion durations from received-signal frequency ratios and requires actual trajectories, endpoints, metric and velocity dependence before comparison. It records future authoring obligations, supplies no new theorem or observation, and retains the primary-report, sampling, calibration and uncertainty requirements. This is the adjudicator check of its repair, not an independent review.

exact_supplier_uses.content: The observers are static with n=f^(-1/2) partial_0, and E_R/E_E=sqrt(f(r_E)/f(r_R)); the scope explicitly requires additional factors for moving observers.
The energy uses n=c^(-1) partial_t, the comoving congruence; E_R/E_E=a(t_E)/a(t_R).

For a piecewise-C1 future timelike segment, proper-time increment is (1/c) times the sum over admissible pieces of integrals of sqrt(-g(gamma_prime,gamma_prime)). Its C1 specialization applies to architecture worldline segments.
Ideal clock reading increments are assumed to equal the proper-time increment of the worldline; this is an adopted physical premise, not an observation.
